html:
The Yindjibarndi are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Pilbara region of Western Australia. Their traditional lands lie along the middle Fortescue River, around Millstream, and they now form most of the Aboriginal community of Roebourne. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were the Ngarluma and Kariyarra toward the coast, the Martuthunira to the west and the Banyjima to the south. Pastoral stations spread over their country from the 1860s, and many Yindjibarndi were moved to Roebourne in the 20th century.

They have fought long legal battles over mining. In 2017 the Federal Court recognised their exclusive native title over a large area that included the Solomon iron ore mine of Fortescue Metals Group, and they later took the company to court for compensation.
